plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flower clusters (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In its native range it grows as a large woody shrub up to 4 meters tall, and it is now widely grown as a holiday potted plant and as a landscape plant in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, grown outdoors in warm regions such as southern California, Florida, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The colorful parts of a poinsettia are modified leaves called bracts, and the plant needs long nights of about 12 to 14 hours of uninterrupted darkness to trigger color development. This is why it blooms near the winter solstice.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant flowers that open from autumn into early winter. It is one of the earliest camellias to bloom and is popular for hedges, espaliers, and woodland gardens in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking, cosmetics, and hair care in Japan and China.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, entire streets and parks turn purple during its bloom, and the fallen blossoms create a violet carpet beneath the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and Brazil
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, earning it the nickname Jacaranda City. In Australia, a local tradition holds that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial that blooms in the depths of winter, bearing nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens above dark, leathery leaves. It thrives in shaded, woodland conditions with alkaline soils and is valued for providing color when little else is in bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family. Folklore tells of a young girl whose tears for having no gift for the Christ child turned into these flowers in the snow.
